results.note: All details verified; my Table 1 sum is 761. Scoring out of 16 is stated on p. 3 and 'no data synthesis' on p. 4 (Methods › Data extraction): worth adding to the locator.

results.corrected_extracted: Twelve trials kept two monitors in the room with the participant for the whole session and one had four; five trials published in 2023 used a single monitor per participant. Rooms were either disguised (living-room style; decorated, pleasant or peaceful; flowers or plants) or left as the hospital environment without particular changes (4 trials); the authors judge the decision to disguise the dosing room rather than amend it to make it more pleasant to have been taken arbitrarily, without evidence-based reasoning. Table 2: a pleasant environment reported by 17 of 25 trials, a monitor present during the session by 18.
results.note: Only the judgment is misplaced: on p. 17 it contrasts disguising the room with amending it to be more pleasant, not with leaving it unchanged. The claim's 'a choice ... made without evidence' carries the same slip. Numbers correct.

Verified in the 4th paragraph: the five reports (three ayahuasca, two labelled DMT, one being 5-MeO-DMT) are open-label without control groups per p. 4; the authors' word is 'suggests', so 'infer' is fair.

All counts verified (p. 9; Table 3 on the rendered p. 13). The review writes 'one study specifically investigated'; 'the one study' sharpens that slightly. Its own description of Kaelen as predictive overstates a correlation; the anchor avoids that.

results.corrected_extracted: Only blood pressure is reported; secondary outcomes are to be published elsewhere. The introduction cites up to 20% of patients receiving intravenous ketamine for treatment-resistant depression as needing medication for treatment-induced hypertension (from a 2021 expert review), but the number treated in each group is not given. The authors suggest that music may be a practical, low-risk, non-drug way to improve the blood-pressure response and name the modest sample as a limitation.
results.note: Facts verified (pp. 1, 3). Overstated hedge: the authors write that music 'may thus represent' a feasible, benign approach; 'present music as' dropped the 'may'. 'Benign' rests only on no serious adverse events being recorded.
